svg.title: iOS · Adjust — New blended clip (video source) · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/AdjustView.swift + App/WarpTimelineView.swift for a video source — the 3a warp timeline, redrawn 2026-08-10 from the iPhone 16 simulator (393×852) after the 2026-08-04 canvas/output-timeline rework and the 2026-08-06 reframe unification left the previous drawing stale. Structure, top to bottom: FlowHeader (back chevron · "New blended clip" · CANVAS MENU chip on the trailing side — the clip's output shape, 16:9 · 9:16 · 1:1 · 4:3 · 3:4, defaulting to the shape as shot; its menu rows carry the consequence, "9:16 — as shot" / "1:1 — crops to 1080×1080", and a non-matching canvas centre-crops the finished clip through VideoCanvasCropper). There is NO source card on the video screen any more (`sourceCard` is the photos branch only) and no SOURCE header row inside the warp card — the card opens straight onto a FULL-WIDTH keyframe preview pane (329×185 at the canvas ratio, aspect-fill, hit-testing off; "≈ keyframe" badge top-trailing, source-clock badge bottom-leading; it no longer chases the playhead, and a tall canvas pins to a 300pt row instead). The Undo chip (and "Fit m:ss" while zoomed) overlays the preview's top-leading corner whenever timeline history exists — see adjust.zoomed.portrait.svg. Below it the stretch bar is drawn in OUTPUT TIME, not source time: each tile's width is its share of the finished clip, so the two ¼× moments here dominate the bar while the 100× base runs between them collapse to 12pt slivers (12pt floor; the surplus is taken back from the wider tiles). Amber tiles when v < 10, accent ring on the selection, speed pills hidden under 30pt, accent resize handles with white grips inside invisible 44pt targets (dragged relatively — no jump-to-finger), a draggable playhead knob, drag-on-the-bar to nominate a 1× stretch (grey-dashed under the 2s minimum then amber; success haptic + "Added 1× stretch · Undo" toast on commit, warning + "Too short" toast below it), pinch to zoom anchored under the fingers to a min(20s, source) floor, double-tap to zoom in/out, hold 0.45s (or right-click on macOS) for Remove · Split here · Reset speed. Seam pills sit under the boundaries ("step" grey; "~1s" ink+amber, 44pt targets, stacked into a second row when two land within 13% of the bar) and open the RAMP AT THIS SEAM popover — duration chips only (step · 0.5s · 1s · 2s); there is NO side choice. Every ease STRADDLES its seam: the compiler splits the sweep at the fast side's renderable floor (outFps÷fps — 1× for base-rate footage), so the fast stretch's footage brakes through everything it can render and lands exactly at the cut, and the sub-floor tail (1×→¼×) plays from the slow side's denser frames — the only footage that can. At the cut both sides render the same real-time cadence, so the speed curve is continuous on screen by construction (this replaced the 2026-08-10 before/after side model the same evening: a side-owned ease pinned its sub-1× tail at the 25fps floor and produced a visible 4× cadence jump at the file cut). Costs fall where they are affordable: the fast side pays ~duration × mean eased speed from its long run; the slow side pays the sub-floor sliver PLUS, at a real file boundary, the post-cut deceleration that bridges the camera's recording hole — ramp-mode format switches lose ~0.6s of real time between files (SourceRegion.leadingGap, estimated from the sidecar's start/end brackets' midpoint + 0.25s bias), and an ease crossing such a boundary raises its split speed so the sweep crosses while per-frame displacement still exceeds the hole (the two frames touching the cut keep the sweep's displacement but consume only its footage part). Displacement per output frame then descends monotonically THROUGH the cut — the hole reads as one ordinary fast frame, not a dropped-frames glitch — at the honest price that the burst funds the visible deceleration, which the compiled captions report truthfully. A stretch eased at both ends offers each seam half its budget, so the first seam compiled can never starve the second. An ease whose neighbours genuinely cannot fund it still clamps, INVERTS the pill into a warning — amber capsule, ink text, labelled with what actually compiles ("~0.2s", "~0s" when it drops below 0.05s and plays as a step) — and the popover carries an accent note ("Only ~0.2s of the ~2s ease fits — the stretches beside this seam are too short for more."). The ruler beneath reads CLIP time (0s · 1:06 · 2:13), not the source clock, and drags to pan a zoomed window 1:1. Then the selection line ("Stretch 2 of 5 · 2:58–3:22 · ¼× slow motion → 1:36 of the clip") with the ⋯ stretch-options button — its "of the clip" number, the tile widths and the clip ruler are all derived from the COMPILED schedule's per-stretch frame counts (eases, clamps and window quantization included), so the stretch captions always sum to the estimate card's total; the steady length÷speed approximation remains only as the fallback while no schedule exists. Outside the card: the fps-gated speed chips (2026-08-11: slow chips need dense footage — ¼× at ≥4× the output rate, ½× at ≥2× — and 50×/60×/100× show only on footage below ¼×-density; 1×/4×/15× and ··· custom always). This ¼×-selected burst stretch shows ¼× · ½× · 1× · 4× · 15× · ···; a base selection shows 1× · 4× · 15× · 50× · 60× · 100× · ···. They always edit the selection, the two-line hint, the PUNCH-IN REFRAME disclosure row ("Off" until the track has keys, then "N keys" in accent-deep — see adjust.reframe.portrait.svg), and the ink estimate card, which the fixed bottom bar clips at this content height (its before/after bar, explainer, Advanced row and Blend-from chips are below the fold). The edit is a monotonic time-warp, never a trim; speeds are ×-real-time; every ease interpolates in LOG-SPEED (equal ease time per halving — a 50×→¼× warp reads as a steady Star-Wars-style deceleration instead of spending nine tenths of the ease looking fast) across 32 constant-speed runs, straddling its seam as described above, and the compiler integrates OUTPUT TIME — each output frame consumes exactly 1/outFps of output time through the piece curve (short ease runs merge, long steady pieces split; a fractional-frame carry keeps Σ windows equal to the frames walked; a region's leftover shorter than half a frame is absorbed into its final frame) — so schedules match the files to the frame and per-frame displacement follows the planned sweep with no rounding artifact beside a cut. The warp axis itself is built from PROBED file durations (CaptureProject.sourceSegmentSeconds), not the sidecar's wall-clock spans, and a stored timeline authored on the older sidecar axis is rebased segment-by-segment on open (AppModel.healWarpAxis) — so estimates equal renders and ease tails no longer starve at end-of-file. Sample data: the LL_ADJUST=demo capture (8:16, two 120fps moments) with LL_STRETCH="0=100,2=100,4=100" and a 1s burst-ramp default, i.e. 100× base runs, ¼× moments, ~1s seams.
